title: Microsoft shares head for worst month since 2000 as AI concerns wipe out $570 billion
description: Microsoft shares are heading for their worst month since 2000, falling 17% in June as concerns over heavy AI spending and delayed returns erased $570 billion in value. Weak Azure growth and high capital expenditure outlook weighed on sentiment, though some investors see value at lower valuations.

title: Yes Bank to raise up to $1.7 billion via equity, debt issue
description: Yes Bank is poised to raise up to ₹160 billion through a strategic mix of equity and debt offerings. The board has approved an equity issuance of as much as ₹75 billion alongside a debt issuance reaching ₹85 billion. This approach is designed to strengthen the bank’s capital framework while minimizing dilution for current shareholders and adhering to regulatory standards.

title: US stocks today: US stocks climb as US, Iran halt attacks; Comcast surges on spin-off plan
description: Wall Street's indices surged on Monday, lifted by a decrease in Middle East tensions and Comcast’s intention to divide into two separate firms. While investors exude cautious optimism amidst ongoing diplomatic developments, regional conflicts still loom large. Anticipation for upcoming earnings reports and uncertainty around AI expenditures contribute to market fluctuations, keeping traders on alert for possible Federal Reserve rate changes.

title: Eswari Global Metal Industries files papers for Rs 1,100-1,300-cr IPO
description: Eswari Global Metal Industries is poised for a major Initial Public Offering (IPO) with an ambitious target of raising Rs 1,100 to Rs 1,300 crore. This strategy entails both a fresh share issuance and an offer-for-sale by existing promoters. The proceeds are earmarked for expanding manufacturing capabilities, clearing debts, and addressing general corporate requirements. The company has showcased impressive financial achievements for the nine-month period concluding December 2025.

title: BSE announces change in licensing requirements for market data products from Jan 2027
description: BSE Ltd has announced a significant transition in its management of international licensing for market data products, effective January 1, 2027. This move sees BSE taking charge from Deutsche Börse AG, which previously handled these operations since their 2013 agreement. Clients outside India, however, will experience no disruption in service, while Indian clients maintain their direct access unchanged.

title: Quote of the day by Dean Williams: "The reason for dwelling on the virtue of simple investment approaches is that complicated ones, which can’t be explained simply, may be disguising a more basic defect. They may not make any sense"
description: Dean Williams' wisdom highlights a crucial investment principle: if a strategy can't be explained simply, it might hide fundamental flaws.  Complex financial jargon can mask risks and flawed logic.  Savvy investors prioritize understanding what they own and why, focusing on clear, fundamental approaches.  Embracing simplicity often proves to be a powerful competitive edge in the market.

title: Omaxe to invest Rs 6,200 cr to build 19 hotels in 5 states
description: Omaxe, a key player in real estate development, has announced a bold initiative involving a Rs 6,200 crore investment over five years to create 19 hotels in five states. This will encompass approximately 5 million square feet of new infrastructure located strategically in urban centers, religious hubs, and major transport routes.

title: Puravankara aims Rs 1,000 cr revenue from 6.4 acre housing project in Bengaluru
description: Puravankara is embarking on an ambitious 6.4-acre residential project in Bengaluru's Sarjapur neighborhood, with projected earnings of Rs 1,000 crore. This project, developed through a collaborative agreement with a landowner, will offer 0.8 million sq ft of saleable space. The company aims to capitalize on the joint development agreement model, minimizing initial investment while diversifying its presence in key urban markets across India.

title: India bonds rise as US-Iran halt strikes; monsoon risk limits gains
description: Indian bonds have surged for the fifth straight session, fueled by easing U.S.-Iran tensions and robust foreign investment. The 10-year yield has fallen to its lowest point since March. However, concerns linger about a widening monsoon deficit in the central region, which could lead to food inflation and dampen market enthusiasm amid the global improvements.
